overview: A weak system brings light snow to the Cascades and Sierra over the weekend. A break Monday is followed by a stronger storm midweek, with the Pacific Northwest and Sierra turning wetter through Thanksgiving week.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: A weak disturbance brings light lowland rain and mountain snow showers Saturday night into Sunday, with little impact expected. A stronger frontal system then arrives Tuesday, bringing snow to the mountains and rain mixing in along the coast. Mt. Baker and Crystal Mountain are in line for the most, with Mt. Baker's total at 15" and Crystal Mountain's at 15".

regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: A weak system crosses the region Sunday, giving light snow above 4000 feet and a few flurries lower down. Monday is dry before a stronger storm arrives midweek, bringing rain to the Valley and snow to the mountains. Forecasters expect less precipitation and weaker winds than the last storm. Sugar Bowl leads with a 13" total, and the NWS is calling for more, 11 to 21 inches Sunday through Wednesday night.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Snow comes early in the week, with a chance of flurries Sunday and Monday. The pattern turns wetter by Tuesday and Wednesday, with rain and showers along the coast. Whistler is forecast 15" over the period, with most of it falling Tuesday and Wednesday.

regions.title: Eastern Sierra
regions.text: Snow showers on Sunday come with a short, fast system that has little moisture, so totals stay modest and the drive home Sunday evening is the main concern. Monday afternoon through Tuesday evening is the best travel window. The next storm arrives Tuesday and brings a longer stretch of snow. Mammoth's total is 9".

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 11, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Nov 22–28. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
